data.description:
Thuy Nu was worried about Chloe. She had to be. It was important to be. The girl was very vulnerable, and so dear to her too. Every day it seemed, to Thuy at least, that the chances of catastrophe were rising higher and higher for her dearest, bestest, friend.

To an outside observer however, one not clued up with the current political climate, social zeitgeist and prevailing morals of the day, the risk - any risk, would appear laughable. Chloe was carefree, smart, inquisitive and excitable. Also, she had a knack for languages and had therefore met Thuy at a Vietnamese-English language exchange on campus. The two as a partnership felt forced at first. One formal, one excitable. Some bright and loud, one calmer, more cautious. But after a jerky start they’d really started to truly melt into each other’s lives. If not quite yet each other's arms. Chloe loved showing Thuy around her little country and even smaller city, while Thuy revelled in their interactions, which were so free of the conformity and obligation she was more used to at home. She could really be herself with Chloe. Maybe even be herself properly for the first time with anyone. This was why it was so important to protect her now. Keep her safe.

Thuy Nu walked down the steps of the university language school, skipping two at a time to hasten her speed, but then stopping as she found she’d stumble more often than not. These steps were not made for people who were only five foot tall in heels! People just like her. She regathered her pace again once she got onto the little path that led through the leafy trees behind the building. She checked her watch. There was no time limit to adhere to though. But, sometimes, once you’d had a certain idea, the thought itself created an immediate need for alacrity not previously present. She sped up a little, knowing she could be only a few minutes away from Chloe’s. Once there she flitted up the unkempt drive of Chloe’s old Victorian student rental. Trying to relax a little the Vietnamese pocket rocket fizzled out at the door and gently knocked with dainty fingers. Chloe answered almost immediately, as if knowing something of grave importance was afoot.

“Thuy, Thuy, come in, come in. I just knew you’d come…”

Thuy melted a little looking into her light brown eyes, and then watched as the much paler, and taller, girls bounded across the living room and started to make two cups of tea in the small kitchenette. This was always the way she tried to diffuse tension. Thuy could never work out how Chloe moved with such speed, yet so much grace. And with so much hair everywhere! Regardless, she was always entranced by it. It was like being friends with an angel or fairy, or long blonde haired elf.

Once tea had been made the two retreated to Chloe’s small upstairs bedroom and sat, one on the bed, and Thuy in a soft armchair crowded with discarded scarves and jackets. The smaller girl studied her friend. Chloe let her take her in for a few moments and then couldn’t stand the polite tension any longer. “What’s up hun, you can tell me. Is it about…you know..?” Chloe couldn’t bring herself to say it, and shuddered a little to even think about it. It was an intense feeling to even contemplate it for a second. It really was.

The smaller girl’s eyes wobbled a little. They were beautiful and dark, like a doll’s, but deadly serious too, behind it all. “Yes, yes, it’s all about that. I’m getting more and more worried. And with you. You are so pretty…” Chloe blushed “...I just think someone will…well. I thought it should be me, first. I thought I should do it. Not them.”

Chloe gulped, but really she had been anticipating this for a while, weeks maybe, longer? At very least she had been waiting in the back of her mind. Maybe even the last few months with Thuy, joking, cuddling, sharing their lives together had just been one long interview leading up to this moment. It was starting to feel like it.

Gently, Thuy opened up her college bag and then placed a small machine on the bedside table. It was about the size of a hand-held waterpistol a child might buy at the seaside, but metallic and slick, clad in a beautiful deep red chrome. Gold letters on the side, in Vietnamese Thuy had taught Chloe to read, said one ominous thing: ‘Shrink Ray’!

More accurately actually it said ‘Little Machine’, but the western popular cultural term had managed to stay, despite their new lack of cultural preeminence. Thuy had bought it before coming abroad for university, as was standard practice for the cultures with un-shrinkable genetics. It kept her safe and gave her status, plus an incredible power to exercise at her leisure. Fortunately, Thuy Nu was far too kind to do so. However, it wasn’t a world full of Thuy Nu’s.

Despite reasonably strict rules being in place internationally for the treatment of the shrinkable races, there weren't any real rules around the application of shrink rays! It was now common for tourists to shrink their own living souvenirs to take back home, or to shrink those in power to get their way. Even some celebrities hadn’t been immune to the ever-growing sound of Zapping! The international students on campus had had an especially hard time resisting the urge. (Mainly as they all had the means in their back pocket!) Amazingly, the tiny local students seemed to be getting quite settled in their new role over the months since the craze began. Thuy even enjoyed that some of her professors were now miniature, while still staying very professional in their roles. It was a credit to the local education system and their cultural dedication to the job, she thought.

What worried Thuy most was the idea that someone, and someone soon, would shrink down her little Chloe and keep her for themselves. The thought really frightened her. It had to be prevented!

Chloe lent forward and gently held Thuy’s small hand. “I totally understand. Honest, I do. I mean, I’ve started running and hiding when the East Asian Society comes past in case they turn me into a mouse or something.” She said being irreverent, but also deadly serious.
